pool.text: The kafu of Bamako was founded by the Niare family.
The Scottish explorer Mungo Park visited Bamako during his exploration.
Gustave Borgnis-Desbordes established a fort at this key strategic location.
A railroad was built connecting Bamako to Kayes.
The city began growing quickly upon being named the capital.
A railroad connecting Bamako to Dakar was completed.
The National Library of Mali was first created by the Institut Français.
It was opened under the direction of Ukrainian archeologist Yuriy Shumovskyi.
The National Museum moved into a new cemented structure.
The Gabriel Touré Hospital was established in the city.
Mali gained independence from France and the Republic was established.
The library was transferred from Koulouba to Ouolofobougou.
Bamako was the location of a WHO conference known as the Bamako Initiative.
The National Congress for Democratic Initiative was set up by Mountaga Tall.
A large-scale protest march in central Bamako was violently suppressed.
Alpha Oumar Konari officially became president of the nation.
The photography festival African Photography Encounters was held in Bamako.
The administrative complex was begun by President Konaré with Libyan funding.
The film was first released at the Cannes Film Festival.
The Bamako city government privatized waste collection in the city.
